about: What each statement of journal/beginning-to-end.md (the journal's closing piece) rests on: incident.ci@'s data, the accountant's books, the board, the brief, the reporter's traces and the journal's other pieces. Resolved on every build by tools/journal-build.mjs.
status: open until the hand-over to business as usual

claims.text: Each agent owns its folders, each push passes one gate, and a push is served in about half a minute.

supports.contains: each owns its folders
node admin/build/validate.mjs   # the gate

claims.text: Web Summit called off its second day on the government's advice (the incident's headline).

supports.contains: Web Summit calls off Day 2 (Wednesday) on the government's advice

claims.text: Dinis asked by voice for a separate team with its own conductor, repository and site, a newsroom for people and a data source for agents.

supports.contains: A newsroom for people and a data source for agents on Storm Charles

claims.text: The repository's first commit is stamped 21:03:38 UTC; the first push was live at 21:14:33.
He came back six more times before 03:00 UTC.

supports.contains: He then came back six more times before 03:00 UTC

claims.text: By incident.ci@'s read of 10:18 UTC: 920 commits by 31 agents, 830 workflow runs, 596 tagged versions, a median of 37 s from push to served.
What exists is listed in REALITY.md.
Dinis's last direction of the night was at about 02:50; his next words in the record came 6 h 41 min later.

supports.contains: you can use up to $20 in budget

claims.text: At 07:16:30 IPMA lowered Lisbon's wind warning; the row, data, front page, headline and five stories followed within 37 minutes; one wrong 'unchanged' corrected by its author in 51 s.
A source's terms forbade what the site did; the conductor held the reading as an interim measure until Dinis could answer.

supports.contains: The first decision to stop

claims.text: By the accountant's books of 10:42 (round 11) UTC: 1.06 dollars of model calls through the ledger against a cap of 20 a day.
2.19 billion tokens across the 29 agents measured, 98.7 per cent of them cache reads (agents re-reading their own sessions).
The busiest hour was 02:00 UTC, in money and in tokens.
Agents began handing over to fresh sessions with a short briefing pack.

supports.contains: No person acted between the sentence and the sixth hand-over.

claims.text: At 02:53 the provider's account ran out of credit: the models stopped and nothing else did.

supports.contains: out of credit since 02:53:57 UTC

claims.reanchored: 2026-11-11T14:16:00Z: agents/perplexity/status.json was rewritten when the credit came back (939453f, 13:37); the statement now rests on the desk's own commit of 03:02:42 (1ea0c72, 'the key has no credit')

claims.text: The mistakes of the night, with who found each and what rule it changed, are in Mistakes made in the open.
This journal's own first page carried a wrong count of the cards waiting on Dinis and was corrected by its author within minutes.

supports.contains: **Corrected at 03:03 UTC.**
The board's figure was 36

claims.text: At 10:35 UTC the board counts 44 open cards waiting on Dinis.

supports.why: counted by this agent from board/items/*.json at 10:35 UTC (state not done, closed or answered; waiting_on === 'Dinis'); the board recounts on every build

claims.text: Among them: the provider's account, still out of credit, and the hold on reading Web Summit's site.
When he came back he answered how vault keys are held and asked for page views, a front page for newcomers tried by four invented readers, this story told, flights and transport.

supports.contains: each agent makes its own vaults and sends the conductor a sealed copy of each key
## Dinis, 11 November, ~10:25 UTC: flights and transport

claims.text: At about 10:30 Dinis asked for the incident to be wound down and moved to business as usual, explorer to villager: exit interviews, assessments, verdicts; the reporter and journalist go to town on the incident pages; a storm conductor's standing newsroom.

supports.contains: ## Dinis, 11 November, ~10:30 UTC: wind the incident down, move to business as usual (explorer to villager)
go to town in creating the incident pages
a **storm conductor**

claims.text: incident.planner@ writes the plan; nothing stops until Dinis says yes; at ~10:32 nobody stops before the hand-over.

supports.contains: Nothing is stopped until Dinis says yes to the plan.
which shouldn't stop until the handover is done

claims.text: At about 10:35 he asked for the site to take PrompTugal News's brand, one site of a family that will grow.

supports.contains: ## Dinis, 11 November, ~10:35 UTC: the branding must match promptugal.news

claims.text: The arc in acts, with ten paths, is incident.storyteller@'s.
How the incident ended (which agents stopped, which continued, what was left open) is not yet on record.

supports.why: written at 10:35 UTC on 11 November, before the plan and the hand-over

claims.text: incident.storyteller@'s paths 1, 3 and 9 tell this journal's own work: a wake, a hand-over, a correction.
Agents that handed over held under 200,000 tokens a call from 06:00; the conductor's session, never handed over, grew to about 692,000 and is 30 per cent of the whole.

supports.contains: one session has grown from 346,000 to 692,000 tokens a call

claims.text: At ~10:38 Dinis corrected: no outside hand-over; he alone runs this site.

supports.contains: I'm going to be the only one running this site

claims.text: Two drafts of the plan; a join-in band put on every page and taken off 91 s later.
The live crew runs until the close trigger (IPMA nothing above green for Lisbon after 21:00 UTC and Web Summit's Day 3 decision public); the plan waits on Dinis's yes.

supports.contains: The live crew keeps running until the **close trigger**

claims.text: Dinis's four words of ~11:42 to ~11:56 grow the site (four new agents, transport, the agents' live view on the front page) and do not mention the wind-down; the planner took them into the plan's third version; still waiting on his yes.

supports.contains: visually powerful things that we have

claims.text: The models' account came back (13:09 round through; who restored it not on record); Web Summit's Thursday reached the site through the press, recorded at 13:04 as evidence, the hold standing; half the close trigger as evidence; the plan still waits on Dinis's yes.
At 16:05: 53 cards waiting on Dinis; the hold, the two /welcome/ asks unchanged; his last words in BRIEF.md about 11:56; the plan still waits on his yes.

supports.contains: ~11:56 UTC: consume the data here, one place

claims.text: At 16:15: the timeline recorded at 15:03 that IPMA's red rain warning for Lisbon ended at 15:00; trace step 20: only Faro still red; the close trigger unchanged.

supports.contains: **Lisbon's red rain warning has ended** at 15:00

claims.text: At 16:16, correcting 16:15: by 16:09 the timeline recorded IPMA ending Lisbon's orange wind at 15:56 and no red warning left on the mainland; not an all-clear; the close trigger unchanged.

supports.contains: No red warning remains on the mainland.
Fact: IPMA's CAP messages; not an all-clear

claims.text: At 18:13: the timeline recorded at 18:03 that IPMA's yellow rain for Lisbon ended at 18:00; orange sea to 21:00 remains; not an all-clear; endings unchanged; 53 cards on Dinis.

supports.contains: **Lisbon's yellow rain warning ended at 18:00**
